title: A Orchard for the Uniform
premise: In 1913, Cyrus Reyes keeps the lighthouse above a coastal town whose orchards and workshops have fed three generations of families whose names exist only in a hand-kept ledger. When the army requisitions the town for the war effort, the ledger — the only proof of who owns what — is seized along with everything else, and the townspeople face erasure from their own history. Cyrus, a widowed outsider who never felt she belonged, discovers her late husband helped copy the ledger and hid a duplicate among the lighthouse's storm records. As the workshop that can authenticate the names is scheduled for demolition, Cyrus rallies the displaced townspeople to finish transcribing the hidden copy, forging an unlikely justice outside the law. The book ends with the army's officer, moved by the completed record, quietly allowing the names into the official register before he ships out — and Cyrus, finally belonging, lighting the lamp as the great storms begin.
about_author: Coral Almeida is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing municipal records in small coastal towns, where she became fascinated by the documents ordinary people leave behind. She writes historical fiction about the quiet custodians of memory, and this is her third novel.

chapters.title: The Lamp Before the Storm
chapters.summary: Cyrus Reyes trims the wick in the lighthouse she has kept alone since her husband Tomás died two winters ago. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: competent loneliness; she believes history happens elsewhere, to other people.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Names
chapters.summary: At the town hall, Cyrus glimpses the old ledger recording every family's claim to orchard land and workshop shares. The clerk jokes no one reads it anymore. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: faint curiosity, the first thread of connection to a town that never fully accepted her.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Water
chapters.summary: A naval cutter appears offshore; soldiers row ashore and post requisition notices on the church door. POV: Cyrus from the gallery of the lighthouse. Emotional beat: dread arriving slowly, like weather.

chapters.title: The Town That Isn't Ours
chapters.summary: The townsfolk argue in the tavern — comply, flee, or resist. Old Marta Vidal insists the ledger proves the land is theirs by right. POV: alternating Cyrus and Marta. Emotional beat: fear hardening into defiance.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Captain Ellery Hargrove arrives to inventory the town. He is courteous, exhausted, and utterly procedural. Cyrus delivers his quarters' lamp oil and hates how reasonable he seems. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: unease at finding the enemy human.

chapters.title: Seized
chapters.summary: Soldiers carry the town hall records, including the ledger, onto a transport barge. Marta weeps openly for the first time in decades. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: grief for paper, which is really grief for identity.

chapters.title: What Tomás Left
chapters.summary: Sorting Tomás's effects, Cyrus finds his handwriting interleaved in the lighthouse's storm logs — a partial transcription of the ledger pages, begun secretly years ago. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: shock, then betrayal curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: The Hidden Copy
chapters.summary: Following Tomás's marginal notations, Cyrus finds oilskin packets behind the lamp room's lead flashing: most of the ledger, copied page by page. It is incomplete. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: awe and terror — she now holds something worth killing for.

chapters.title: Time Already Running Out
chapters.summary: Hargrove announces the workshop will be demolished within six weeks; its press and seals are the only means of authenticating restored documents. POV: Hargrove. Emotional beat: duty grinding against private doubt.

chapters.title: An Orchard for the Uniform
chapters.summary: Marta tells the story of the title: soldiers once took the orchard's fruit and left nothing, and the ledger was created so it could never happen again. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden and gift.

chapters.title: Recruiting the Faithful
chapters.summary: Cyrus gathers a small circle — Marta, the blacksmith's widow Ines, teenage apprentice Rolo — and shows them the hidden pages. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: terrified trust extended for the first time since Tomás died.

chapters.title: Rolo's Eyes
chapters.summary: Rolo, who idolizes the soldiers, struggles between admiration for Hargrove and loyalty to the circle. POV: Rolo. Emotional beat: adolescence as a battlefield of loyalties.

chapters.title: Copying by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Nightly transcription begins in the lighthouse, disguised as storm-log work. Cyrus teaches Ines Tomás's shorthand. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: fragile hope, hands learning a dead man's habits.

chapters.title: The First Inspection
chapters.summary: A sergeant nearly discovers the packets during a routine search of the light station. Cyrus bluffs using her keeper's authority. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: adrenaline, then shaking aftermath.

chapters.title: Hargrove's Ledger
chapters.summary: Hargrove reviews the requisition accounts and finds discrepancies suggesting someone above him is profiting from seized property. POV: Hargrove. Emotional beat: the crack in the uniform.

chapters.title: The Missing Pages
chapters.summary: The circle discovers entire sections are absent from Tomás's copy — including the workshop families' claims. Someone else may hold them. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: despair at incompleteness.

chapters.title: The Clerk's Confession
chapters.summary: The dying town clerk admits he sold duplicate pages to a quartermaster before the requisition. POV: the clerk. Emotional beat: shame seeking absolution too late.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Barometers fall; the first of the great storms approaches, and with it a supply ship carrying the quartermaster who bought the pages. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: nature and fate converging.

chapters.title: The Quartermaster
chapters.summary: Cyrus trades lamp oil and harbor knowledge to get close to Quartermaster Brandt, who wears the missing pages folded in his coat like a talisman. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: revulsion at bargaining with a vulture.

chapters.title: What the Sea Takes
chapters.summary: The first great storm hits; the supply ship founders on the shoals. Cyrus runs the light through the worst night of her life. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: terrible clarity — she saves the man who stole from her town.

chapters.title: Salvage Rights
chapters.summary: Brandt, half-drowned and grateful, is nursed in the town he helped strip. Ines refuses to speak to him. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: mercy as an act of will, not feeling.

chapters.title: The Bargain
chapters.summary: Brandt, shaken by the wreck and Hargrove's questions about his accounts, agrees to return the pages in exchange for silence about his profiteering. POV: Brandt. Emotional beat: cowardice choosing the safer crime.

chapters.title: Pages Restored
chapters.summary: The recovered sections arrive, water-stained but legible. Rolo deciphers the hardest passages. POV: Rolo. Emotional beat: the boy earning his place among adults.

chapters.title: The Workshop Still Stands
chapters.summary: With two weeks left, the circle must use the workshop's press and seals to authenticate the full transcription — under the soldiers' noses. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: audacity born of desperation.

chapters.title: Daylight Forgery
chapters.summary: Marta walks into the workshop openly, claiming she's been ordered to crate its contents, and prints authentication seals while guards help her carry boxes. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: triumph disguised as obedience.

chapters.title: A Crack in the Circle
chapters.summary: A neighbor, resentful that his family's claim was denied in the original ledger, threatens to inform. POV: the neighbor. Emotional beat: justice complicated by old wounds — the ledger itself wasn't fair to everyone.

chapters.title: The Question of Fairness
chapters.summary: The circle debates whether to restore the ledger exactly or amend its old injustices. Cyrus argues for truth over comfort; Marta disagrees bitterly. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh — inheritance includes inherited wrongs.

chapters.title: Hargrove Suspects
chapters.summary: Hargrove notices fresh ink on 'crated' documents and confronts Cyrus at the lighthouse. She neither lies nor confesses; he leaves without arresting her. POV: both. Emotional beat: two honest people on opposite sides of a dishonest order.

chapters.title: Demolition Order Moved Up
chapters.summary: A telegram moves the workshop demolition forward by ten days. Someone informed after all — or Hargrove's superiors grew suspicious of him. POV: Hargrove. Emotional beat: the walls closing in.

chapters.title: Last Printing
chapters.summary: Through one frantic night the circle completes and seals every page in the workshop while demolition crews sleep. Rolo nearly breaks his arm under a falling beam. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: exhausted, sacred labor.

chapters.title: Betrayal
chapters.summary: The resentful neighbor reports the circle. Soldiers surround the lighthouse at dawn. Cyrus burns nothing — instead she hands Hargrove the finished record and dares him to read it. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: defiance as surrender to a higher law.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Hargrove spends the night reading names, cross-checking against his own requisition lists, and sees the theft of a whole town rendered in ink. POV: Hargrove. Emotional beat: conscience arriving like dawn.

chapters.title: Arrests
chapters.summary: Marta, Ines, and Rolo are detained pending transport. Cyrus is confined to the light station — the army still needs the lamp lit. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: guilt of the free, fury of the caged.

chapters.title: Brandt's Choice
chapters.summary: Facing exposure regardless, Brandt testifies to his own profiteering and confirms the ledger's authenticity, implicating officers above Hargrove. POV: Brandt. Emotional beat: self-interest accidentally becoming courage.

chapters.title: The Officer's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Hargrove must choose: destroy the record and obey, or enter it into the official register and end his career. He requests a hearing. POV: Hargrove. Emotional beat: a good man betting everything on procedure bending toward justice.

chapters.title: The Hearing in the Hall
chapters.summary: In the requisitioned town hall, the circle testifies; Marta speaks the names aloud until the room stands. Hargrove enters the record into the register before witnesses. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: catharsis — history reclaimed in public.

chapters.title: Costs
chapters.summary: Hargrove is relieved of command and ordered away; the demolition proceeds anyway, though the authenticated record survives in triplicate. The neighbor asks forgiveness and receives silence, not absolution. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: victory that does not feel like winning.

chapters.title: Departures
chapters.summary: The army withdraws ahead of the second great storm. Hargrove says goodbye at the lighthouse door; Cyrus gives him a single pressed orchard blossom from Tomás's copy packet. POV: both. Emotional beat: tenderness without promise.

chapters.title: The Second Storm
chapters.summary: The great storms arrive in earnest. The town shelters together in the stone workshop they couldn't save, reading the new ledger by lantern light as wind tears at the coast. POV: ensemble. Emotional beat: belonging forged in shared peril.

chapters.title: Lighting the Lamp
chapters.summary: Spring. The register bears the town's names; the workshop is rebuilt around its surviving press; Rolo apprentices as keeper's boy. Cyrus lights the lamp at dusk, no longer a stranger, and begins writing the next ledger herself. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: inheritance accepted — history, she now knows, happens here, to us.
